comments.body:
RCA (rebar-debug, Phase 1 complete).

ROOT CAUSE (one cause, two consumer sites): commit 8f4c5fdb0d3 (ticket 1d22-40ba-8e2b-4f67 / dragonish-sylphic-sheep, 'Preserve OpenAI Chat Completions semantics', 2026-08-17) made rebar's resolver canonicalize every openai-family model spec to the 'openai-chat:' qualifier (src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py:246-269) and updated the UNIT-tier matrix gate with a family->qualifier mapping (_MODEL_QUALIFIER_BY_PROVIDER, tests/unit/test_ci_provider_matrix.py:73), but never updated the LIVE external tier's consumers of the provider name — an unmet consumer update, not a defect at the failing site:
1. tests/external/test_provider_matrix_live.py:71,87,94 compare resolved specs / configured_provider() LITERALLY against REBAR_EXPECTED_LLM_PROVIDER='openai' (the matrix.provider family name) -> the observed AssertionError at line 88.
2. tests/external/_live_llm.py:46-50: _PROVIDER_KEY_ENV has no 'openai-chat' entry, so configured_provider()='openai-chat' -> credential_present() False -> live_llm_ready() False -> EVERY llm_live test on the openai arm skips ('no live LLM: configured provider is openai-chat but its credential is absent'). This is why the whole live suite never ran (15s job).

PROOF (runtime oracle, no live credentials): local run with REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1 REBAR_EXPECTED_LLM_PROVIDER=openai REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE=.github/llm-providers/openai.toml OPENAI_API_KEY=<dummy> reproduces the CI failure byte-for-byte (AssertionError, line 88, same resolved dict) plus 3 skips naming 'openai-chat ... credential is absent'. Transition anchored in run history: openai arm SUCCESS on run 32000764439 (head 81c3e9ec, does NOT contain 8f4c5fdb) and FAILURE on 32308848370 (head 9bfe4b42, DOES contain 8f4c5fdb).

RIVALS KILLED: (b) 'openai.toml wrong' — rejected: the unit gate updated in the SAME commit requires the overlay to use openai-chat: (tests/unit/test_ci_provider_matrix.py test_each_overlay_sets_only_the_model_selection_keys), so the spec grammar side is the contract. (c) 'pydantic-ai upgrade renamed the provider' — rejected: the prefix is produced by rebar's own _resolve_target (git log -S openai-chat names 8f4c5fdb0d3, rebar code, not a lockfile bump), and the good->bad transition matches that commit exactly.

DEFECT LEGITIMACY: defect (regression via unmet obligation), test-tier only. The guard's documented intent (module docstring: 'the arm ran the provider it claims') is still satisfied — openai-chat and openai 'name the same provider family' per the introducing commit's own comment at model_classes.py:247. The arm's resolved specs ARE the declared provider, so the failure is a guard false positive; regression evidence: green run 32000764439 before the change. The fix maps qualifier->family in the live tier; it does NOT change which provider the arm runs, and the guard keeps its teeth (a class resolving to a DIFFERENT family still fails).

CAUSED_BY (date test applied): the guard predates the transition (added 2026-08-03, commit 9af278b01fc, epic f124); the behavior became wrong 2026-08-17 with 8f4c5fdb0d3. Attribute to the change that created the obligation and shipped without updating its consumers: ticket 1d22-40ba-8e2b-4f67. Close class: regression.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
Live External Integration run 32568560934, job 'external LLM (live openai)', failed in 15s: tests/external/test_provider_matrix_live.py:88 (test_every_model_class_resolves_to_the_declared_provider) asserts each model class resolves with the literal prefix 'openai:' but the resolver now canonicalizes openai specs to 'openai-chat:' — and the rest of the live suite silently skipped because tests/external/_live_llm.py's credential map has no 'openai-chat' entry, so live_llm_ready() is False on the arm. Root cause proven (see RCA comment): commit 8f4c5fdb0d3 (ticket 1d22-40ba-8e2b-4f67) renamed the openai qualifier to 'openai-chat' and updated the unit-tier matrix gate (_MODEL_QUALIFIER_BY_PROVIDER, tests/unit/test_ci_provider_matrix.py:73) but not the live external tier — an unmet consumer update. The arm's specs ARE openai-family, so the guard failure is a false positive.

## Approach
Teach the live external tier the same family/qualifier distinction the unit tier already has (mirroring _MODEL_QUALIFIER_BY_PROVIDER at tests/unit/test_ci_provider_matrix.py:73, introduced by the same commit that created the obligation), in one place:
- tests/external/_live_llm.py: add a qualifier->family map ({'openai-chat': 'openai', 'openai-responses': 'openai'}) and a provider_family() helper; configured_provider() returns the FAMILY name, so credential_present() (keyed 'openai' -> OPENAI_API_KEY at _live_llm.py:46-50), live_llm_ready(), _skip_reason(), and the guard's equality at test_provider_matrix_live.py:94 all agree with the workflow's REBAR_EXPECTED_LLM_PROVIDER=matrix.provider family name.
- tests/external/test_provider_matrix_live.py: the two literal startswith(f'{_expected}:') comparisons (lines 71 and 87) compare provider FAMILY of the resolved spec's qualifier (via _live_llm.provider_family) against the declared arm provider instead. The guard keeps its purpose: a class resolving to a DIFFERENT family (e.g. anthropic on the openai arm) still fails.
- tests/unit/test_ci_provider_matrix.py: add unit-tier regression tests over _live_llm (via the existing _live_llm_module() path-import helper at tests/unit/test_ci_provider_matrix.py:441) pinning: with the openai overlay (.github/llm-providers/openai.toml) and OPENAI_API_KEY present, configured_provider() == 'openai' and live_llm_ready() is True. These run in ordinary CI (no live credentials), so the regression is caught before a live run.
This fixes the guard test itself because the current assertions encode the stale literal comparison (the test asserts the bug); per the debug protocol the revised guard is re-verified RED against the unfixed _live_llm before the fix lands. No production (src/) code changes; the resolver's openai-chat canonicalization is the contract side (enforced by the unit gate) and is untouched.

## Scope
- tests/external/_live_llm.py — qualifier->family mapping + provider_family(); configured_provider() returns the family.
- tests/external/test_provider_matrix_live.py — family-based comparisons in the two guard tests.
- tests/unit/test_ci_provider_matrix.py — unit regression tests for openai-arm readiness and family mapping.

## Testing
- RED first: new unit tests fail on current main (configured_provider() returns 'openai-chat', live_llm_ready() False); captured before the fix. Local replication of the CI failure (REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1 REBAR_EXPECTED_LLM_PROVIDER=openai REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE=.github/llm-providers/openai.toml OPENAI_API_KEY=<dummy>, no live calls in this module) fails at line 88 exactly as in run 32568560934.
- GREEN: after the fix the same replication command passes the guard module (region test self-skips), and the new unit tests pass.
- Failure path kept: mutation check — restoring the literal comparison / removing the openai-chat family entry returns the oracles to RED; pointing the overlay at anthropic.toml on a declared-openai arm makes the guard fail (guard retains teeth).
- Full gates: make lint, make typecheck, python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check, and the unit suite.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Root cause proven per rebar-debug (mechanism + discriminating experiment) with defect_legitimacy citing the guard's documented intent vs the spec grammar — RCA comment on this ticket (done, see comment 1).
- [ ] caused_by attributed via git history date test to 1d22-40ba-8e2b-4f67 (guard predates the qualifier rename); recorded via --caused-by on the close.
- [ ] Fix lands RED->GREEN: unit regression tests seen failing on unfixed tree, passing after; the live-openai guard module passes locally by driving the resolution path without live credentials (replication command above).
- [ ] Parity sweep: anthropic and bedrock arms checked for the same prefix fragility — both flow through the same provider_family() seam after the fix; verified by running the guard module locally under each arm's overlay env; any residual fragility filed + linked discovered_from.
- [ ] Gates green: make lint, make typecheck, complexity baseline --check; change merged via Gerrit with LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1.

file_impact.reason: add qualifier->family mapping; configured_provider returns the provider family so credential lookup and arm equality work for openai-chat
guard compares provider family of the resolved qualifier against the declared arm provider instead of a literal prefix
unit-tier regression tests: openai overlay yields configured_provider()==openai and live_llm_ready() True with the key present
